<backend><forward-request /></backend> ever runs. No request, no

The lifeline above is drawn deliberately empty." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="88" width="420" x="694" y="990" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="p-takeaway" parent="1" style="rounded=1;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#666666;fontColor=#000000;fontSize=11;align=left;verticalAlign=top;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=6;" value="Fourth surface on the ADR-006 error taxonomy
This surface now has three instances: the issue-17 per-server 403,
the issue-88 id-validity 400 (step 4b), and the per-tool deny below.
Two of the three change the HTTP status, so ADR-006's "only tier 1
changes the status" holds within tiers 1-3 ONLY, never system-wide.
A gateway-side per-tool denial is a JSON-RPC Protocol Error:
HTTP 200 carrying an error object, with the request id echoed.
It is NOT a transport 401/403 ahead of the JSON-RPC envelope
(that tier is reserved for transport and session violations), and
NOT a CallToolResult with isError=true (that tier is reserved for
failures during actual tool execution).
-32001 is a custom code in the MCP-reserved range (-32000 to
-32099), deliberately not -32602 'Unknown tool', which would
misdescribe a mapped-but-under-entitled caller.
MCP spec 2025-06-18; COMPATIBILITY.md 2026-08-06." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="190" width="520" x="40" y="1120" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="p-ordering" parent="1" style="rounded=1;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#666666;fontColor=#000000;fontSize=11;align=left;verticalAlign=top;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=6;" value="Two causes, one indistinguishable wire response
An unmapped tool name and a mapped-but-under-entitled caller
produce the SAME response; it does not say which. The audit
event carries the tool name for operators who need to tell them
apart.

Audit ordering is a constraint, not a style choice
<trace> is documented for inbound, outbound and backend only,
never for on-error, so it must sit in <inbound> immediately before
the deny <return-response>. severity=error is the maximum tier of
the verbosity enum, so it clears the diagnostic setting's gate
(severity >= configured verbosity) at ANY configured verbosity -
a robust relationship, not a fragile exact-match one. COMPATIBILITY.md 2026-08-07." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="190" width="520" x="580" y="1120" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="p-legend" parent="1" style="rounded=1;fillColor=#f7f7f7;strokeColor=#999999;fontColor=#000000;fontSize=11;align=left;verticalAlign=top;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=6;" value="Arrows
blue solid = request
purple dashed = HTTP 200 + JSON-RPC error
teal dashed = audit telemetry, side channel

The blue and purple arrows carry the same
meaning here as in mcp-request-outcomes
(ADR-006); the teal one is new to this
diagram and is not a client-visible response.

Faded lane = present but never invoked." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="190" width="340" x="1120" y="1120" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="p-step4b" parent="1" style="rounded=1;fillColor=#fff8e1;strokeColor=#e8820c;strokeWidth=1.6;fontColor=#1a1a1a;fontSize=11;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=10;spacingRight=10;" value="4b. Id-validity guard (issue #88) - BEFORE the map lookup, so it applies whatever that lookup would have decided
valid id = present AND not null AND (string OR integer). MCP 2025-06-18: "Requests MUST include a string or integer ID", and
"Unlike base JSON-RPC, the ID MUST NOT be null". Invalid -> return immediately; the map lookup below never runs." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="74" width="520" x="230" y="640" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> </mxfile>

g.text: Per-tool authorization: the deny path
Phase 3.5 thickening (issue #18) plus the id-validity guard (issue #88), ADR-009. Extends v1.0.0; mid-implementation - live-gate proven but NOT merged. NOT part of the v1.0.0 tag.
What happens AFTER the issue-9 and issue-17 checks pass: the id-validity guard (step 4b, issue #88) and the per-tool deny (issue #18). The allow and fall-through paths are deliberately not drawn.
MCP client
holds a valid, server-entitled token
API Management (MCP gateway)
per-tool authorization, in <inbound>
MCP server Function App
backend - not reached on this path

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(232, 240, 251), rgb(26, 33, 43)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(108, 142, 191), rgb(92, 121, 163));

g.text: Application Insights
audit sink (side channel)
Persistent and out-of-band: a separate
resource group, outside the ephemeral s2
apply/destroy lifecycle, reached by a
cross-resource-group APIM logger.
Precondition - already passed before this diagram starts

path.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(47, 91, 156), rgb(129, 167, 223)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(47, 91, 156), rgb(129, 167, 223));

g.text: 1. tools/call - JSON-RPC 2.0 request {id, method, params.name} + bearer token

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(238, 247, 238), rgb(22, 29, 22)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(130, 179, 102), rgb(68, 110, 44));

g.text: ALREADY PASSED - not this diagram's subject
- no-token check: HTTP 401 + RFC 9728 challenge (issue #9)
- validate-azure-ad-token: issuer, audience, allowed client application ids
- per-server entitlement: scp 'X.Invoke' OR roles 'X.Invoke.All', else HTTP 403 insufficient_scope (issue #17)

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 246, 230), rgb(32, 24, 11)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(232, 181, 102), rgb(116, 73, 5));

g.text: Per-tool authorization (issue #18) - all of it in <inbound>, before <backend>

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 255, 255), rgb(18, 18, 18)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(108, 142, 191), rgb(92, 121, 163));

g.text: 2. Parse the JSON-RPC body ONCE
context.Request.Body.As<JObject>(preserveContent: true) into mcpRequestBody, then mcpMethod.
Request body only. context.Response.Body is the one that breaks MCP streaming; it is never read.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 255, 255), rgb(18, 18, 18)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(108, 142, 191), rgb(92, 121, 163));

g.text: 3. Gate on the JSON-RPC method
mcpMethod == tools/call ? No -> fall through unchanged (tools/list, initialize, everything else).

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 255, 255), rgb(18, 18, 18)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(108, 142, 191), rgb(92, 121, 163));

g.text: 4. Resolve the tool name - two mechanisms (ADR-009)
primary: the gen_ai.tool.name context variable
fallback: mcpRequestBody.params.name, used only if that variable is empty

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 255, 255), rgb(18, 18, 18)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(108, 142, 191), rgb(92, 121, 163));

g.text: 5. Total-map lookup against this server's tool_authorization_map
case unrestricted -> allowed (it already cleared the per-server check above)
case scope / role -> scp.Contains(scope) OR roles.Contains(role)
default -> allowed = false: a tool name with NO map entry is denied

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(253, 238, 238), rgb(39, 27, 27)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(184, 84, 80), rgb(215, 129, 126));

g.text: 6. allowed == false -> DENY (the only branch this diagram depicts)

path.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(232, 130, 12), rgb(190, 103, 1)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(232, 130, 12), rgb(190, 103, 1));

g.text: 4c. HTTP 400 + JSON-RPC error, id key OMITTED (there is no valid id to echo, and inventing one
would break the caller's correlation) {jsonrpc: 2.0, error: {code: -32600, message: Invalid Request ...}}
NO audit event: nothing was denied, and every id-less tools/call gets identical bytes, so there is no enumeration signal to record.

path.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(0, 131, 143), rgb(58, 171, 181)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 131, 143), rgb(58, 171, 181));

g.text: 7. ONE audit event: <trace source=issue-18-per-tool-authorization severity=error>
metadata: caller (oid, else azp, else unknown) and tool. Not sampled - every deny is recorded.
8. HTTP 200 + JSON-RPC Protocol Error, request id echoed
{jsonrpc: 2.0, id: 7, error: {code: -32001, message: insufficient_scope ...}}

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(253, 238, 238), rgb(39, 27, 27)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(184, 84, 80), rgb(215, 129, 126));

g.text: BACKEND NEVER INVOKED ON THIS PATH
The deny <return-response> sits in <inbound> and returns before
<backend><forward-request /></backend> ever runs. No request, no
forwarded token and no tool execution reaches the Function App.
The lifeline above is drawn deliberately empty.
Fourth surface on the ADR-006 error taxonomy
This surface now has three instances: the issue-17 per-server 403,
the issue-88 id-validity 400 (step 4b), and the per-tool deny below.
Two of the three change the HTTP status, so ADR-006's "only tier 1
changes the status" holds within tiers 1-3 ONLY, never system-wide.
A gateway-side per-tool denial is a JSON-RPC Protocol Error:
HTTP 200 carrying an error object, with the request id echoed.
It is NOT a transport 401/403 ahead of the JSON-RPC envelope
(that tier is reserved for transport and session violations), and
NOT a CallToolResult with isError=true (that tier is reserved for
failures during actual tool execution).
-32001 is a custom code in the MCP-reserved range (-32000 to
-32099), deliberately not -32602 'Unknown tool', which would
misdescribe a mapped-but-under-entitled caller.
MCP spec 2025-06-18; COMPATIBILITY.md 2026-08-06.
Two causes, one indistinguishable wire response
An unmapped tool name and a mapped-but-under-entitled caller
produce the SAME response; it does not say which. The audit
event carries the tool name for operators who need to tell them
apart.
Audit ordering is a constraint, not a style choice
<trace> is documented for inbound, outbound and backend only,
never for on-error, so it must sit in <inbound> immediately before
the deny <return-response>. severity=error is the maximum tier of
the verbosity enum, so it clears the diagnostic setting's gate
(severity >= configured verbosity) at ANY configured verbosity -
a robust relationship, not a fragile exact-match one. COMPATIBILITY.md 2026-08-07.
Arrows
blue solid = request
purple dashed = HTTP 200 + JSON-RPC error
teal dashed = audit telemetry, side channel
The blue and purple arrows carry the same
meaning here as in mcp-request-outcomes
(ADR-006); the teal one is new to this
diagram and is not a client-visible response.
Faded lane = present but never invoked.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 248, 225), rgb(30, 24, 4)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(232, 130, 12), rgb(190, 103, 1));

g.text: 4b. Id-validity guard (issue #88) - BEFORE the map lookup, so it applies whatever that lookup would have decided
valid id = present AND not null AND (string OR integer). MCP 2025-06-18: "Requests MUST include a string or integer ID", and
"Unlike base JSON-RPC, the ID MUST NOT be null". Invalid -> return immediately; the map lookup below never runs.
